reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
It's a Monday in the back half of August. The light is starting to slant differently in the evenings — you can feel fall leaning in, even if the days still run hot. This is the kind of day that used to disappear on me. Nothing dramatic, nothing worth remembering, just another Monday to grind through until I could turn it off. And that was most of my life, actually. A long string of Mondays I wasn't really present for.

What sobriety gave me — and I didn't understand this at 22 — is that the ordinary days are the whole thing. Not the ski trips, not the summits, not the big weekends. Those are the highlights. The real life is the coffee at 6am, the drive to work, the workout you didn't feel like doing, the text you actually answered. Durant's point, borrowed from Aristotle, is that you become what you do over and over. Not what you intend. Not what you post. What you actually repeat.

So today isn't small. Today is where the person you're becoming gets built, one boring choice at a time. Show up for the Monday. Answer the email. Make the bed. Go to the meeting or the gym or the walk. The extraordinary life people talk about is just a stack of ordinary days someone didn't skip.
reflection.meditation: What is one small, ordinary thing I can show up for fully today?

affirmations: I am building my life in the ordinary hours, not waiting for the big ones.
Today I get to choose my response instead of react on autopilot.
I am becoming someone I can live with, one honest day at a time.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful for a Monday I actually get to be present for. Grateful for the version of me that white-knuckled through the early days so I could have this one — coffee in a quiet kitchen, a body that works, people who know my real name. The small stuff isn't small. It's the whole inheritance.
gratitude.closing: One more day, clear-eyed. That's the win.
